characters.summary: Geralt is a mutated witcher, a monster slayer for hire, who fights with a sword in either hand-style fast and strong attacks, casts the five witcher Signs, and drinks alchemical potions within a toxicity limit.

techniques: Fast and strong sword attacks (strong attacks ignore armor)
Igni: a gush of flame
Aard: a telekinetic wave that throws back, knocks down or stuns
Yrden: a magical ground trap that wounds and immobilises
Axii: briefly turns an enemy into an ally

mechanisms: Mutations give high resistance to injury, poison and disease

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources (no opponent-exploitable weakness documented on the opened pages)
limitations: Signs cost Stamina; when it runs out he must rely on Adrenaline to cast (Witcher 3 skills)
Potions add Toxicity; drinking past his overdose threshold is limited

sources.supports: Witcher mutations from the Trial of the Grasses give high resistance to injury, poison and disease; monster slayer for hire; horse Roach; faces the Wild Hunt in The Witcher 3.
What each of the five Signs does (Aard, Igni, Yrden, Quen, Axii); Signs cost vigor/stamina. Descriptions quoted there are from The Witcher 2; the same five Signs are used in The Witcher 3.
The Witcher 3 skill trees: fast and strong sword attacks, strong attacks ignore armor, parry deflects arrows, Signs via Stamina or Adrenaline, potion Toxicity and overdose threshold.
Main quest 'On Thin Ice': Geralt kills Caranthir and then Eredin, king of the Wild Hunt, aboard Naglfar.

feats.claim: Slew Eredin, king of the Wild Hunt, "with his own hands" aboard Naglfar after killing the navigator Caranthir.
feats.citation: Witcher Wiki: 'On Thin Ice' (journal entry and walkthrough)

notableResults.note: Killed in the final battle aboard Naglfar; the allied force fought the Hunt as a whole, but the journal credits Geralt with slaying Eredin himself.
Walkthrough steps "Defeat Caranthir" and "Kill Caranthir" before boarding Naglfar; fight details not given.

campaignTags.claim: Casts the five witcher Signs in combat.
Igni Sign projects a gush of flames that wounds opponents.
Aard Sign is a telekinetic wave that throws back, knocks down or stuns.
Axii Sign makes an enemy fight at his side as an ally for a short while.

unknowns: Sign descriptions on the Witcher Wiki Sign page are quoted from The Witcher 2; Witcher 3 skill data confirms the same Signs but exact Witcher 3 effects were not separately quoted.
Removed (not supported by opened sources): meditation requirement for brews; "higher vampires" feat; Roach not tagged mount (a horse grants no flight).
No opponent-exploitable weakness documented on the opened pages.

characters.continuity: Street Fighter II (with Street Fighter Alpha 3 backstory)
characters.summary: Guile is a United States Air Force major and one of the original eight World Warriors, who fights with the projectile Sonic Boom and the anti-air Flash Kick to avenge his friend Charlie against M. Bison.

techniques: Sonic Boom (projectile)
Flash Kick (anti-air; knocks down opponents who do not block)

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Flash Kick has slow recovery, leaving him open if it misses or is blocked
limitations: Sonic Boom and Flash Kick are charge moves: a direction must be held briefly before release
Only one Sonic Boom can be on screen at a time

sources.supports: Wikipedia (Wikiwand mirror): USAF major; Sonic Boom and Flash Kick; seeks to avenge Charlie against M. Bison; one of the original eight World Warriors of Street Fighter II.

Giant Bomb: Street Fighter II ending (defeats Bison, then backs off rather than kill him); Alpha 3 (learns Charlie's style, escapes the Shadaloo base with Chun-Li); Sonic Boom and Flash Kick mechanics, charge inputs, Flash Kick recovery.

notableResults.note: Street Fighter II ending: Guile defeats Bison and has the chance to kill him, but hesitates and backs off.

unknowns: Removed (not supported by opened sources): generic "defeated high-level martial artists" feat; "trained martial arts guard" defense; Street Fighter V continuity (the sourced material is Street Fighter II and Alpha 3).
USAF rank alone does not earn pilot; no piloting feat documented.

characters.summary: Illidan Stormrage is the first demon hunter: a blinded night elf who sees through mystic-fire eyes, wields the Warglaives of Azzinoth and fel magic, and in Legion returns to kill Gul'dan and the naaru Xe'ra before becoming Sargeras' jailor.

techniques: Warglaives of Azzinoth
Fel energy (tore Gul'dan apart with it)
Demon hunter Eye Beam and Throw Glaive (class signature abilities; Illidan is the first demon hunter)

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
mobility: Unfolds demonic wings for gliding descents; double jump and vault (demon hunter abilities)
limitations: His eyes were burned out by Sargeras; he sees through orbs of mystic fire that perceive magic (spectral sight)
Demon hunters must keep their inner demon in check; Metamorphosis risks the demonic power taking over

sources.supports: Illidan's history: Warglaives of Azzinoth, eyes burned out by Sargeras and replaced with mystic-fire orbs, Legion: kills Gul'dan with fel energy at the Nighthold, kills Xe'ra on Argus, becomes Sargeras' jailor.
Illidan is the first demon hunter; demon hunters' spectral sight, warglaives, Metamorphosis, wing gliding, Eye Beam and Throw Glaive, and the risk of the inner demon taking over.

feats.claim: Killed the naaru Xe'ra on Argus after she bound him in Light and tried to forcibly infuse him with it.

notableResults.note: Nighthold: after the heroes defeat Gul'dan, the reawakened Illidan kills him with fel energy, the same way Gul'dan killed Varian.
Argus: killed her after breaking free of her attempt to infuse him with the Light.

campaignTags.claim: Wields fel magic; tore Gul'dan apart with fel energy.
Demon hunters unfold their wings to perform gliding descents; Illidan is the first demon hunter.

unknowns: Eye Beam, Throw Glaive and gliding are documented as demon hunter class abilities; they are attributed to Illidan because he founded the class.
Removed (not supported by opened sources): fel fireballs, magical wards, "susceptible to magical displacement", true wing flight (only gliding is documented), Fel Rush description.
The Nighthold Gul'dan kill follows the heroes defeating him; it is not a solo duel.

characters.continuity: Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne onward (World of Warcraft demon hunter Metamorphosis)
characters.summary: Illidan's demon form, first gained by consuming the power of the Skull of Gul'dan, gives him horns, wings and hooves; in it he wrapped himself in shadow and destroyed the dreadlord Tichondrius and his forces.

techniques: Shadow and fel power drawn from the Skull of Gul'dan
Warglaives of Azzinoth

mechanisms: Not established by the cited sources

weaknesses: Not established by the cited sources
mobility: Demonic wings; demon hunters glide on them
characters.formDifferences: Demon form gained from the Skull of Gul'dan: demonic horns, wings and hooves, fel tattoos, and the power that destroyed Tichondrius. Size and exact strength gain are not documented on the opened pages.

sources.supports: Illidan consumes the Skull of Gul'dan's power, is transformed into a demon, wraps himself in shadow and destroys Tichondrius and his forces; in The Frozen Throne he has demonic horns, wings and hooves.
Demon hunter Metamorphosis transforms them into hellish forms; risk of the demonic power taking over; wings used for gliding.

unknowns: Removed (not supported by opened sources): "towering" size, thick hide, self-regeneration, fel aura, true flight, time limit on the form.
Continuity changed from Legion: the documented demon-form feat (Tichondrius) is from Warcraft III.
limitations: Metamorphosis carries the risk that the demonic power takes over and the elf is lost

notableResults.note: Warcraft III: newly transformed by the Skull of Gul'dan, Illidan "utterly destroyed Tichondrius and his forces".

campaignTags.claim: Demon hunters unfold their wings to perform gliding descents; the demon form has wings.

characters.summary: Isabelle, the Animal Crossing secretary, fights only in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate, using everyday items: a party popper, a fishing rod that grabs from range, the Lloid Trap, a Pocket that catches projectiles, and a balloon bench to recover.

techniques: Party popper (forward smash, her most reliable KO option)
Fishing Rod: grabs and throws opponents from farther than her normal grab
Lloid Trap: a planted gyroid that fires when an opponent walks over it

mechanisms: Pocket: catches an opponent's projectile and can fire it back

weaknesses: Light and floaty, so she is easy to launch and struggles to return to the ground safely
Balloon Trip recovery is among the most easily edgeguarded
mobility: Balloon Trip: rides a swinging bench under two balloons for long vertical and horizontal recovery

sources.supports: SmashWiki: Isabelle's special moves (Pocket, Fishing Rod, Balloon Trip, Lloid Trap), party popper forward smash, lightweight and floaty build, slow mobility, easily edgeguarded recovery.

unknowns: She has no combat depiction in Animal Crossing itself; all combat data is Smash gameplay. Continuity changed from Animal Crossing: New Horizons to Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
Removed (not supported by opened sources): clipboard smack, "administrative authority" defense, Villager result.
Balloon Trip is not a glide or flight and earns no tag.

characters.summary: Jigglypuff is a light, floaty balloon Pokemon that puts nearby opponents to sleep with Sing and lands a single hard hit with Rest, at the cost of falling asleep itself.

techniques: Sing: puts nearby opponents to sleep (longer the more damaged they are)
Rest: falls asleep and deals a single hard hit to opponents touching it
Rollout: chargeable rolling slam
Pound: punch with large shield damage

mechanisms: Five midair jumps for aerial evasion
Light, floaty body that is hard to combo

weaknesses: Very light, so it is knocked out at low damage
Instantly KO'd if its shield is broken
Rest has extremely high ending lag and is easy to punish if it whiffs
limitations: Second-lowest weight and jump force in the game

sources.supports: SmashWiki: Jigglypuff's special moves (Rollout, Pound, Sing, Rest), five midair jumps, light weight and floatiness, shield-break KO, Rest ending lag.

unknowns: Removed (not supported by opened sources): "knocked out heavy opponents" feat, inflating to cushion impacts, Mario result.
Multiple midair jumps are not flight or glide; no tag.

characters.summary: Jill Valentine is a former S.T.A.R.S. member trained in marksmanship, bomb disposal and lock-picking who fights with knives, firearms and grenades, dodges at close range, and destroys Nemesis with a prototype railgun.

techniques: Combat knives, firearms and grenades
Marksmanship trained under Chris Redfield
Prototype railgun (final Nemesis fight)

mechanisms: Dodges incoming attacks at close range

weaknesses: Ordinary human vulnerable to infection: Nemesis infected her with the T-virus and she needed Carlos's vaccine
limitations: No superhuman powers; relies on weapons and equipment

sources.supports: Resident Evil 3 (2020): Jill uses combat knives, firearms and grenades and can dodge at close range; defeats Nemesis, is infected with the T-virus, eliminates Nemesis with a railgun and escapes with Carlos.
Resident Evil Wiki: Jill excelled in bomb disposal and lock-picking, could dismantle intricate explosives in minutes, and trained in marksmanship under Chris Redfield.

feats.claim: Survived Raccoon City and escaped by helicopter with Carlos after the vaccine cured her T-virus infection.

notableResults.note: Defeated it earlier but was infected; in the final fight she eliminates Nemesis with a prototype railgun.

unknowns: Removed campaign tag gadgets: lockpicks and standard military gear are standard equipment, not gadget tech (by analogy with the standard-issue armor ruling).
Removed (not supported by opened sources): body armor, first-aid sprays/herbs, incendiary grenades specifically, limited-ammunition weakness.
